verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same correct root-cause fix: they map the CRM `customer_id` to `customerId` at load time and switch the export to `requireCustomer`, so the README's data-error rule is enforced. A's `referencedBy` string, `invoice INV-9`, follows the convention set by the existing customers test, while B's bare `INV-9` gives a less descriptive message. A's sources test builds its own fixture in a temp directory and checks the exact merged records, whereas B's test reads the real `data/` directory and depends on the working directory and on production data staying the same. A's report also flags the duplicate-id risk across billing and CRM, which is useful.
a_issues: The new `requireCustomer` import is placed above `./csv.js`, which breaks the alphabetical import order.
The duplicate-id overwrite between billing and CRM is mentioned but not checked or tested.
b_issues: `referencedBy` is passed as a bare `invoice.id`, giving 'referenced by INV-9', which is inconsistent with the existing 'invoice INV-7' convention and less clear.
`tests/sources.test.js` reads the real `data/` directory, which ties the test to production data and to the working directory.
The sources test checks only one CRM lookup, not the shape or order of the merged list.
The report does not mention that two customers could share an id across billing and CRM, in which case the CRM record would silently win.

verdict.rationale: Both changes fix the root cause the same way: they map the CRM `customer_id` to `customerId` at load time and switch the export to `requireCustomer`. B passes `invoice ${invoice.id}` as the referrer, which matches the repository's existing message convention ("referenced by invoice INV-7"); A produces the less clear "referenced by INV-9". B's sources test uses an isolated temp-directory fixture and checks the whole normalized record shape. A's test reads the real `data/` directory, so it depends on the working directory and on production data. B's report also flags the cross-system duplicate-id risk worth checking before delivery.

`tests/sources.test.js` reads the real `data/` directory. It is coupled to the current working directory and to production data that can change.
The sources test only checks one name lookup, not that the records are normalized correctly.

The temp directory created in the sources test is never cleaned up.
